claims.claim: For every fixed threshold τ≥2, a simple three-occurrence color sequence encodes a spanning forest with exactly two roots, even root degrees, and odd nonroot degrees.
claims.evidence: Let the board have N=2n vertices and q=n−1 colors, each with three stacks of height τ−1. In any play empty after the prefix, the first two stacks of a color must be nonadjacent: otherwise 2(τ−1)≥τ eliminates them and leaves the sole remaining stack, of height τ−1<τ, permanently present. Hence the first phase occupies exactly N−2 distinct vertices. On its final occurrence, each color must be placed at an empty common neighbor of both surviving stacks; adjacency to fewer than both leaves at least one stack. Orient the resulting two graph edges from that empty center to the cleared pair. Every initially occupied vertex receives exactly one parent, while the two initial vacancies receive none. A nonroot center was cleared strictly earlier than its children, so parent-to-child clearing times strictly increase and cycles are impossible. There are N−2 edges, hence exactly two rooted tree components. Each use of a center adds two children, so roots have even degree and nonroots have one parent plus an even number of children, hence odd degree.
claims.search_method: Direct invariant and temporal-order proof; additionally enumerated every successful clearing schedule on all 32,834 labeled simple graphs with 2, 4, or 6 vertices using integer bit sets.

claims.claim: For the leaf-corona G of a connected subcubic graph H, the above prefix can empty G if and only if H has a Hamiltonian path.
claims.evidence: In the two-root parity forest, a pendant root has degree zero, while every nonroot pendant vertex has its unique edge present. For |V(H)|≥2 both roots cannot be pendant, since they would be two isolated components with vertices left over. If neither is pendant, deleting all pendant edges leaves two forest components in H; in each, its root has odd degree and every other vertex even degree, contradicting the handshaking lemma. Thus exactly one root is a pendant a′ and is isolated; the other root r is original. Removing all pendant vertices leaves a spanning tree T of H. If r=a, every T-degree is even, impossible for a nontrivial tree. Otherwise precisely a and r have odd degree. Since H is subcubic, all other vertices have degree two in T; the tree degree sum forces deg_T(a)=deg_T(r)=1, so T is a Hamiltonian path. The one-vertex case also satisfies the equivalence directly. Conversely, from a Hamiltonian path v1,…,vn, leave v1′ and vn empty, put color ci on the nonadjacent pair v_{n−i+1}′,v_{n−i}, and clear these pairs successively at centers v_{n−i+1}. Every center is initially empty or was cleared by the preceding move, and the final configuration is empty.
claims.search_method: Parity and handshaking proof in both directions, supplemented by exhaustive exact comparison of Hamiltonian-path existence and prefix clearability for every connected labeled subcubic graph on 1–5 vertices.

claims.claim: Fitting Hexasort is NP-hard for every exact fixed threshold τ≥2, even on graphs of maximum degree four.
claims.evidence: Reduce from Hamiltonian Path on connected maximum-degree-three graphs. The leaf-corona has maximum degree at most four, and Claim 1 proves that its prefix ends empty exactly for Hamiltonian source instances. Append N one-occurrence colors of height one to the N-vertex board. For τ≥2 these fresh stacks cannot merge or vanish and each permanently consumes one empty vertex. If k vertices are occupied after the prefix, only N−k suffix stacks can be placed, so all N fit exactly when k=0. The graph and sequence have polynomial size, and fixed τ uses only the constant heights τ−1 and 1. This gives the required many-one reduction for every exact fixed τ≥2.
claims.search_method: Audited both directions of the reduction, the suffix-capacity argument, fixed-threshold quantifiers, construction size, and maximum degree; checked the capacity identity exactly for board sizes 1–32.

claims.claim: Complete classification: the constant-threshold problem is NP-complete for every fixed τ≥2, while τ=1 is trivial.
claims.evidence: A certificate lists one chosen vertex per input stack. Each deterministic placement and same-color merge can be simulated with polynomially many integer operations, so Fitting Hexasort is in NP. Claim 2 supplies NP-hardness for every fixed exact τ≥2, proving NP-completeness. It also resolves the target's bounded interpretation: for every fixed upper bound T≥2, instances with t≤T contain the NP-hard exact-t=2 subclass and remain in NP. For T=1, every positive-height stack immediately reaches threshold when placed, so any sequence fits on a nonempty graph; only a nonempty sequence on an empty graph fails. Thus threshold one is polynomial-time trivial.
claims.search_method: Certificate-size and simulation analysis, exact/bounded-threshold quantifier check, and direct analysis of the threshold-one boundary case.

target_evidence: The exact target asks for the complexity of Fitting Hexasort when t is bounded by a fixed constant. The draft proves the stronger exact-threshold dichotomy—NP-complete for every fixed τ≥2 and trivial for τ=1—and explicitly observes that every bounded restriction t≤T with fixed T≥2 is NP-complete through its exact-t=2 subclass. The Empty-style prefix is correctly converted to Fitting Hexasort by the permanent N-stack suffix. Thus the entire requested classification is established at the requested strength, and claimed_resolution FULL is accurate.
checks_performed: Read only the designated source-input JSON and baseline-draft JSON; did not use the web, retrieval data, prior runs, or verification reports.
Checked the target against the final result, including the distinction between exact fixed τ and the promise t≤T.
Proved symbolically that τ−1<τ and 2(τ−1)≥τ for every integer τ≥2.
Reconstructed and verified the two-root forest invariant, its acyclicity, component count, and degree parities.
Audited every root-placement case in the leaf-corona argument, including the one-vertex edge case.
Audited both directions, polynomial size, fixed-height values, suffix forcing, and maximum degree in the NP-hardness reduction.
Ran the persisted exact-integer checker: all 368,738 successful clearing schedules found across 32,834 labeled graphs satisfied the forest invariant.
Ran exact exhaustive comparison on all 516 connected labeled subcubic graphs with 1–5 vertices; Hamiltonian-path existence and prefix clearability agreed in every case.
Verified NP membership and the τ=1 and bounded-threshold boundary cases.
